questions.q: What is the actual constraint driving Priya Nair's push for a fast rollout?
options: She simply dislikes the security team and wants to undermine the program
There is one planned maintenance outage window on the calendar, and missing it means either a six-month delay or an unplanned outage with its own real operational and safety costs
She has a personal deadline unrelated to Hartwell's operations
The board ordered her to ignore all security requirements
questions.explain: Priya's position comes from a real, concrete scheduling constraint, not carelessness — missing the window has a genuine, costly consequence.

questions.q: Why does Mara Voss insist the corrected audit methodology must apply to the new segment from day one, even under time pressure?
options: Because she personally enjoys slowing down projects
Because deploying without time to validate the new methodology risks recreating the same kind of blind spot Lesson 19's AAR documented, now on equipment with physical stakes
Because the board explicitly forbade any OT segment expansion
Because Priya Nair has no legitimate reason to want speed
questions.explain: Mara's concern is specific and well-founded: a compressed validation window could let a new version of the exact documented gap go unnoticed for months.

questions.q: What happens, concretely, if Operations simply wins this conflict outright?
options: Nothing changes about risk; the rollout is identical either way
The rollout ships inside the window with validation compressed or skipped, and if the new segment has its own blind spot, nobody finds out until the next scheduled audit months later
Hartwell loses its zero-trust pilot results entirely
Priya Nair is immediately removed from her role
questions.explain: The real risk of an uncontested speed-first approach is repeating the original incident's exact failure mode — a gap sitting unnoticed for months — on a segment with physical consequences.

questions.q: What happens, concretely, if Security simply wins this conflict outright?
options: The rollout proceeds exactly on schedule with no downside
The rollout slips past the maintenance window, costing six months of delay or an unplanned, costly outage, and risks the program being seen as blocking a funded, board-approved initiative
Priya Nair's department is dissolved
The audit methodology from Lesson 19 becomes unnecessary
questions.explain: An uncontested caution-first approach has its own real cost: delay, expense, and reputational risk to the program's credibility going into the next budget cycle.

questions.q: Why is this conflict described as structurally harder than the Beginner and Intermediate capstones' stakeholder tensions?
options: Because Priya Nair and Mara Voss have never met before this lesson

Because the earlier tensions turned out to be compatible asks that one well-scoped project satisfied, while this one pits a real deadline against a real validation requirement over the same calendar window
Because this is the first time the capstone has involved more than one stakeholder
Because the earlier conflicts never involved Mara Voss directly
questions.explain: Earlier tensions resolved through reconciliation once both asks were understood; this one requires an actual compromise, since the two needs are genuinely in tension over the same fixed window.
